title: Do Internationalised Universities Make Regions Richer? Pre-Registered Panel Evidence from European NUTS-2 Regions, 2013–2022
content:
Regional policy often presents the recruitment of foreign students as a lever for local2
development, but regional-level evidence is scarce. This study tests whether European3
NUTS-2 regions whose higher-education institutions enrol a larger share of foreign students4
subsequently reach higher real GDP per capita. Institution-level data from the European5
Tertiary Education Register (ETER) are aggregated to regions and linked with Eurostat6
regional accounts. The analysis plan was fixed before estimation. The pre-registered7
specification is a two-way fixed-effects panel with region and country-by-year effects,8
covering 1,922 region-years in 216 regions of 21 countries (2013–2022). A one-percentage-9
point higher foreign-student share in the previous year is associated with 0.090% higher10
real GDP per capita (95% CI−0.077 to 0.257; p= 0.290). Alternative outcomes, lags,11
subsamples, measures and the absolute number of foreign students give similar null results.12
Only a cross-sectional long difference is positive (p= 0.014); its variation lies between13
regions over a decade, not within regions. Shift-share instruments are weak, so no causal14
claim is made. The hypothesis is not supported at this scale and horizon. That is not15
evidence of no economic value: a calibration shows that a NUTS-2 annual panel cannot16
detect the local demand effects single institutions plausibly generate
